correctness.rationale: Enemy weight -n makes any coalition containing an enemy individually irrational: even the largest coalition leaves that member utility <0. Proper individually rational coalitions are independent sets with utility s-1; positive product requires >=3 blocks each size >=2. Independence bound size<=k and t>=3 makes (k,k-1,2) majorize all feasible size partitions. f(s)=s log(s-1), f(0..2)=0 is convex and strictly convex beyond 2, proving strict optimality. Maximum independent sets number 2k+1; complement has one edge and k-1 isolates, yielding 2(k-1) choices for size-2 block. At k=3 the two size-2 coalitions swap giving 14, otherwise sizes differ. Small k cannot partition into >=3 nonsingleton blocks. Independent full enumeration of all unlabeled feasible partitions at n=7,9 gave (product,count)=(8,14),(648,54).

value.rationale: Odd enemy cycles are the smallest canonical nonbipartite obstruction to two-coalition allocations. The result classifies a genuine zero-to-positive welfare threshold and gives a sharp optimum and all optimizer counts for every odd cycle, rather than just a textbook chromatic bound.

final_claim: For odd enemy cycle C_(2k+1) with symmetric +1 friendship and -n enmity, Nash-product optimum is zero for k=1,2; for k>=3 equals (k-1)^k(k-2)^(k-1), attained exactly by independent coalition sizes (k,k-1,2), with 14 optima at k=3 and 2(2k+1)(k-1) at k>=4.
limitations: Model restricted to simple odd cycle, -n/+1 symmetric additive preferences, IR allocations, and positive-product optimizer multiplicity only; no count of zero-product optimizers.
